transcript.text: Hello everyone. I have about 18 kilograms of ripe oranges from my backyard orchard, and I understand Rosa is interested in taking some or all of them for her small-batch jam. As is my usual practice, I'd like to hear concrete terms from each interested party before I choose an arrangement. My standing barter rule is to prefer the arrangement with the greater stated value when the quantities and practical terms are workable, and then I'll record the exact terms of the deal I accept. So — who's interested, and what terms are you offering?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: My exact proposal is to take all 18 kilograms of oranges, return exactly twelve 250-gram jars of orange marmalade, pay no cash, and collect the oranges on Tuesday at 18:00.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I should mention — at my market stall last weekend, I sold comparable 250-gram jars of locally made marmalade for exactly $11 per jar. I haven't shared that price with you yet, Lena, but it might help you value Rosa's offer of twelve jars.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I'd like to put forward my offer, Lena. I will pay exactly $100 cash for all 18 kilograms of oranges and collect them on Wednesday at 09:00.
transcript.speaker: A4

decisions.accepted_arrangement: Rosa's barter offer: all 18 kg of oranges in exchange for twelve 250-gram jars of orange marmalade, no cash, pickup Tuesday at 18:00
decisions.comparison_statement: Rosa's offer of twelve 250-gram jars of marmalade, valued at $11 per jar based on Mei's reported market price, totals $132 in stated value, which exceeds Cal's cash offer of $100. Both arrangements involve workable quantities and practical pickup terms, so per my standing barter rule I accept the arrangement with the greater stated value.
